text:
Mia Chen: Heads up — I'm going to start a small canary for the new prompt redaction heuristics this afternoon. Want ops + platform eyes on sampling & quota impact before we flip.

Alex P.: +1. What are the heuristics again? partial redact, keep first token, hash rest?

Mia Chen: Roughly: keep prompt metadata, redact free-text user prompts using token-aware boundaries, then store a keyed HMAC for provenance. We also want an opt-in temporary unmask flow for support with TTL.

Rajesh: How will this affect our telemetry? need tagging so dashboards can distinguish redacted vs unredacted traffic (and which redaction version).

Mia Chen: plan is to add envelope fields in logs: ``pii_redaction=prompt_v2`` and ``redact_hash_v=1`` plus ``unmask_ttl`` when set. Will also attach ``sample_rate`` for sampled captures. Example log envelope:```json
{"pii_redaction":"prompt_v2","redact_hash_v":"h1","sample_rate":0.01,"unmask_ttl":"1h"}```

Diane: small ask: console needs a visible badge that indicates whether a request was redacted and which policy applied. Otherwise support will be chasing ghosts.

Sam: for the temporary unmask flow, please ensure audit trail + one-click revoke. We can't leave unmask tokens around. TTL should be short and revokable.

Alex P.: quota math — if we enable sampled capture for 1% of requests during canary, what's the extra tokens/storage? rough numbers please.

Mia Chen: quick calc: current host requests ~120k/day. 1% sampled => 1.2k captures/day. avg capture size 12KB => ~14MB/day = trivial for short canary. But note we also store HMACs & metadata, so multiply by 1.1.

Rajesh: ok but watch spikes during replay/debug. Ops: can we grant short-term burst quota to the canary org for the next 48h?

ops-bot: @ops:quota-request canary-org +burst 48h requested by mia.chen — awaiting approval.

Diane: UX rollout plan: add a console toggle (admins only) that switches between redact v1 and v2 for a given tenant. Default v1. Canary tenants opt into v2. We need telemetry events for toggles.

Sam: Security checklist: KMS keys used for HMAC must be tenant-scoped where possible; otherwise we need strong access auditing. Also require manual approval for unmask enable.

Alex P.: one more: sampling & privacy. If a tenant opts out of telemetry, sampled captures must honor that. Keep sample honoring consent a hard requirement in code path.

Mia Chen: agreed. Implementation notes I'm putting in the PR — will tag everyone. plan: canary rollout to 5 tenants at 13:00 UTC, sample_rate=0.01, unmask disabled initially, enable only with manual support ticket.

Rajesh: can we add a dashboard panel that shows: redaction-policy, sample-rate, sampled-capture-count, avg-capture-size, unmask-requests? even simple heatmap will help.

Diane: I'll mock the console badge + dashboard widgets this morning. Alex, can we include a saved query for SLOs so we can see latency diff?

Alex P.: yes. quick perf estimate: redaction adds ~3-6ms CPU per request for token parsing; should be fine. We'll watch p50/p99.

ops-bot: @ops:quota-request canary-org +burst 48h — approved by ops-team at 6167778895.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for redaction-service at 6167778896 by mia.chen — see /deploys/6167778896 for logs.

Mia Chen: thanks everyone. if anything odd shows up (latency or unexpectedly high sampled captures), ping me immediately and we'll roll back. planning to capture minimal fields only.

Sam: noted. will follow up with the audit flow and revoke endpoint docs.

Rajesh: tagging this for analytics: we'll store a minimal provenance row referencing the HMAC key id and redact version so we can audit without storing PII.

Diane: moving to UX follow-up thread after this. good to go for canary once deploy completes. :thumbsup:

Alex P.: ack. monitoring alerts going live for redaction-canary p99 > 300ms and sample_count > 2k/day.

Mia Chen: closing loop — will post canary report in #eng-platform in 24h.
